anchor.title: I Want YOU for U.S. Army (Uncle Sam)
anchor.creator: James Montgomery Flagg
anchor.caption: J.M. Flagg's 'I Want YOU' (1917). The poster turned civic and military service into a personal call — a reminder that citizenship carries responsibilities, not just rights.
anchor.alt_en: Cartoon: I Want YOU for U.S. Army (Uncle Sam) (James Montgomery Flagg, 1917).
anchor.alt_es: Imagen: I Want YOU for U.S. Army (Uncle Sam) (James Montgomery Flagg, 1917).

anchor.title: The Third-Term Panic (elephant/donkey)
anchor.creator: Thomas Nast
anchor.caption: Thomas Nast's 1874 cartoon popularized the Republican elephant and Democratic donkey — the two-party system that now runs the presidential nomination process.

anchor.title: The Yellow Press
anchor.creator: L.M. Glackens
anchor.caption: L.M. Glackens's 'The Yellow Press' (1910) shows sensational newspapers shaping opinion — a classic lesson in how media influences which issues seem to matter.

anchor.title: Woman Suffrage Parade, Washington D.C.
anchor.creator: LOC (photographer unknown)
anchor.caption: The 1913 Woman Suffrage Procession: citizens demonstrating and petitioning for the vote — participation that reaches well beyond the ballot box.
anchor.alt_en: Photo: Woman Suffrage Parade, Washington D.C. (LOC (photographer unknown), 1913).
